strategy.summary: Reproduce the GH-63278 near-minimum-timestamp Period construction failure in the millisecond branch of npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime by building the buggy revision e49e355cad46 from source and running the parametrized test_construction_from_min_timestamp; the [ms] case should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime on the buggy build and pass once the PR's scale_time_with_underflow_check helper is applied. The bug lives in C code, so an editable rebuild is required for each revision.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) with make/ninja available for meson
pinned_because: NumPy: no documented constraint and no era table entry, so the NumPy version is a free choice; pick a NumPy release that is installable for the chosen Python and that the buggy commit's test suite runs against, and record that choice here rather than treating it as documented
python-dateutil: unbounded and not numerically relevant; use the latest release compatible with the chosen Python
tzdata: documented as required only on Windows/Emscripten; not needed on Linux
Cython: documented as required for source installs; version is an unbounded choice (use the version the pandas build requires at that commit)

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/period/test_period.py::TestPeriodConstruction::test_construction_from_min_timestamp[ms] (parametrized over freq in ['ms', 'us', 'ns']; the [ms] id is the one expected to fail on the buggy revision)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision e49e355cad46 (rebuilt), the [ms] case of test_construction_from_min_timestamp raises pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime during Period(Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms'), freq='ms') and is reported as FAILED. On the fixed revision (buggy commit plus the PR changes, rebuilt), the same test id passes with no exception, and the [us] and [ns] cases pass on both revisions.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timestamp.min.value (NPY_MIN_INT64 region) interpreted as milliseconds, passed through npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime with base unit NPY_FR_ms; check that the buggy build raises the checked_mul overflow and the fixed build does not.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime (overflow error for -290308-12-21 19:59:05 as cited in the regression test failure)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Successful construction of the Period with no exception

risks: The reproduction depends on a compiled C extension: the buggy and fixed revisions must each be rebuilt (editable install) or the test will silently run the old binary; a stale build can make both revisions look identical.

The fixed revision is not identified by a hash in the evidence; it is the PR's merged state on top of e49e355cad46, so the exact fixed commit must be taken from the PR, and the PR date field is empty.

The failing case is expected only for [ms]; the [us] case may already pass on the buggy revision (the prior GH-63278 test covered us), and the [ns] case has a removed special path, so its buggy behaviour is not confirmed by the evidence.
Passages are diff fragments and may be truncated, so the exact helper body is not fully visible; the reproduction relies on the test diff, not on the helper internals.

Integer overflow behaviour is platform-independent in the C checked_mul path, but a 32-bit or non-Linux build (e.g. Windows, which also needs tzdata) was not evidenced and is not assumed; the transition should be checked on Linux x86_64 with a standard 64-bit int64 long.
No sanitiser or special threading or BLAS configuration is evidenced; none is assumed.

NumPy and Python versions are unbounded in the evidence; a NumPy version whose datetime C API differs from the era of the buggy commit could change whether the bug appears, so the chosen NumPy must be recorded and checked against the buggy failure.

oracle.why: The check is whether construction raises; no numeric tolerance applies, so the oracle is an exception-free transition.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy build, Period(Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms'), freq='ms') goes through the unguarded scaleSecondsToMilliseconds checked_mul(seconds, 1000) path, which overflows for near-minimum values and raises pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime, so the test body raises and pytest reports the [ms] case as FAILED.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed build, scale_time_with_underflow_check splits the scaling as a*(x+k)+(b-a*k) with checked operations that stay in range, so construction returns a Period with no exception and the [ms] case PASSES.
